parsed.explanation: Combined regime: no entry bar for LGBTQ travellers as such, but mandatory original photo ID at transit checkpoints (fines up to 3,000 local currency, detention warnings) is a universal document exposure that initiates police contact. Documented police stops and background checks of about 20 trans women in the largest city (Aug 2025) show state-implicated targeting. Detention is birth-sex based (a trans man in a women's prison), with documented strip searches, isolation and a contested custody death (Dec 2025). No anti-discrimination or gender-identity protection exists, and hormone therapy is unfunded. Rule-of-law recourse is weak: complaints are ineffective and the 2008 record is dated. Rated in the Elevated band, below the 0.35 anchors, because custody-by-birth-sex with documented harm and state-run ID-check stops are traveller-facing. No capital or statutory criminalisation of gender identity is documented.

entry_documents.exposure: Original photo ID required at transit checkpoints in holiday destinations; fines up to 3,000 local currency and detention warnings for non-compliance. Universal for every visitor.
entry_documents.protection: No visa, entry or border condition applies to LGBTQ travellers as such.
entry_documents.interaction: ID checks are the mechanism that initiates police contact; a presentation-document mismatch can convert a routine check into documentation and detention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Aug 2025: about 20 trans women stopped, held at a district police station and released after background 'general information gathering' checks. Prisons hold trans people by registered sex; a trans man was held in a women's prison. Documented strip searches, solitary isolation and restricted healthcare.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Detainees were released without charge or fine. Lawyers' Article 5 challenge is unresolved.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor detained through ID checks would enter the prison system placed by birth or registered sex, with the custody harms above.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National prison system manages trans prisoners by segregation and isolation, not gender-matched placement. Short-term police holding conditions for trans detainees are not sourced.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Opposition MP raised the custody case in parliament; rights groups in six cities demanded investigation. No operative remedy documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Nationally run prisons and transfers apply the same registered-sex regime to visitors and residents alike.

care_services.exposure: Hormone replacement therapy is not covered by the state system; visitors must pay privately. A provincial circular reshaped medical-board reporting nationally, with risk of profiling.
care_services.protection: Surgery is available in several major cities at age 18 or over.
care_services.interaction: Care access depends on private payment and on whether documentation is routed through the gender-reassignment category.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Head of government's rhetoric frames LGBTQ people as a threat to children and the family. Draft package described as effectively criminalising LGBT people; enforcement actions against an association (April 2026) and raids (Sept 2026). Enactment of the draft package is unresolved.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No documented operative official protection for trans people.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat framing raises the likelihood that police and prison staff treat outed visitors as targets.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. The record gives no sourcing on minors travelling with guardians or on family-status scrutiny.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor travelling with a trans guardian would be exposed to the same ID checks and any resulting police contact, but the record does not specify consequences.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2024 knifing of a trans woman; perpetrator released while victim referred for arrest, described as detention asymmetry. 2025: 313 violations, 6 deaths linked to anti-LGBTQ violence (3 hate killings), disproportionately trans. Counts are documented cases, not total incidence.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Documented prosecution of attackers is not shown. Rights organisations document cases.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response is documented as skewed against victims, so reporting is discouraged.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination law covering gender identity; no direct legal protection. Complaints in prisons are ineffective. Pending case since 2023 on remedies. Border screening, passport-marker flagging and anatomy inspection are not documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Partial: 2026 reform removed some discriminatory provisions; no statute protects gender identity in operation.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Border practice is unknown and must not be inferred either way; the Article 5 challenge and draft package status are unresolved.

anchor_checks.comparison: Anchor 0.35-A has a universal, state-run register that refuses entry to trans visitors with no remedy. This dossier has no entry bar and no register, so it sits above 0.35-A. It is comparable in that both rely on discretionary ID checks, but it lacks the entry-denial regime.

Anchor 0.25-C has birth-sex prison housing, cross-dressing arrests and no effective remedy. This dossier shares the birth-sex custody regime, documented isolation and an ineffective complaint process, but has no documented cross-dressing offence. It is close to 0.25-C and therefore slightly higher.

Anchor 0.55-C has birth-sex ward placement with partial denial and a functioning ethics route. This dossier has documented custody harm and a death, with no working remedy, and documented state-run stops, so it sits below 0.55-C.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller-facing exposure is a chain: the universal ID check at transit points initiates police contact, police have documented stops and background checks of trans women, and detention places trans people by registered sex, where isolation, searches and a contested death are documented. Hormone access must be paid for privately. Official threat framing and the 2024 asymmetry case show weak recourse. Border screening, short-term holding conditions and minor-specific rules are undocumented and carry no weight.
